questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of head or neck injury?

options.text: By wearing a helmet.
By riding more slowly.
By reading the owner's manual.

questions.correctAnswerText: By wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Head and neck injuries are always a risk when riding a motorcycle. Wearing a good helmet greatly reduces this risk.

questions.question: Which material gives the best protection in a crash?

options.text: Denim
Leather or synthetic materials
Wool

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather or synthetic materials
questions.explanation: Leather or synthetic materials protect riders best during a crash. Wear long pants and jackets made of these sturdy materials when riding.

questions.question: What should you do when the lights on this sign are flashing?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Proceed with caution.
Turn around and find an alternate route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: What should a rider's boots or shoes do?

options.text: Be below their ankles.
Cover their ankles.
Be made of soft, flexible material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover their ankles.
questions.explanation: Choose sturdy boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: How is alcohol different from other substances?

options.text: It enters the bloodstream very quickly.
It needs to be digested before entering the bloodstream.
It can improve your riding ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: It enters the bloodstream very quickly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested. It passes directly through the stomach and small intestine walls into the bloodstream, quickly affecting your brain.

questions.question: How should jackets and pants fit when riding?

options.text: Loose enough for wind to catch the fabric.
Snug enough to keep from flapping in the wind.
Tight enough to prevent any movement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snug enough to keep from flapping in the wind.
questions.explanation: Your jacket and pants should fit snugly so they don't flap in the wind. They should still be loose enough to let you move freely.

questions.question: What color clothing should you wear when riding during the day?

options.text: Bright colors to help other drivers see you.
Any color, because drivers can easily see you in daylight.
Dark colors to stand out against the bright sun.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright colors to help other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Always wear bright colors to be more visible, even during the day.

questions.question: Is it easy to judge distances when riding at night?

options.text: Yes, easier than during the day.
About the same as during the day.
No, it is harder than during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is harder than during the day.
questions.explanation: Judging distances is harder at night than during the day. Shadows and light help you see distances in daylight. At night, artificial lights can distort or hide these helpful visual clues.

questions.question: When riding in the left third of a lane behind a car, what is a problem?

options.text: Most drivers don't check their side mirrors often.
Wind can prevent the use of side mirrors.
Side mirrors should not be used by motorists.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers don't check their side mirrors often.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. Ride in the center of the lane where the driver is more likely to see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: This is a traffic sign with white background and red and black markings. It tells drivers what they cannot do. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When traveling at night, you should:

options.text: Ride at the same speed as you would during the day.
Ride slower than you would during the day.
Ride faster than you would during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than you would during the day.
questions.explanation: Ride slower at night, especially on roads you don't know well. Riding slower gives you more time to avoid hazards when you can't see as well.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should:

options.text: Keep a safe distance between each rider.
Ride as close to each other as possible.
Not worry about the distance between riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance between each rider.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation when riding in a group. This allows riders to stay close together while keeping safe distances between them.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always wear a jacket.
Wear a jacket only at night.
Wear a jacket only when it is cold.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket.
questions.explanation: Always wear a sturdy jacket with long sleeves when riding a motorcycle, even in warm weather.

questions.question: To reduce the chances of a collision, a motorcycle rider should:

options.text: Keep a safe space cushion around your motorcycle.
Ride very slowly.
Ride on the centerline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe space cushion around your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Always keep space between your motorcycle and other vehicles. Keep this space when following others, being followed, passing, or being passed.

questions.question: To make it easier for other drivers to see you, you should:

options.text: Wear bright-colored clothing while riding.
Wear dark-colored clothing while riding.
Wave your arms while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright-colored clothing while riding.
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors when riding. This makes it easier for other drivers to see you at any time of day.

questions.question: Traffic lanes moving in the same direction are separated by:

options.text: White lines.
Yellow lines.
Road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: A sign that your rear tire has suddenly gone flat is:

options.text: The back of your motorcycle is swaying from side to side.
You hear a loud noise.
Air is visibly coming out.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back of your motorcycle is swaying from side to side.
questions.explanation: If your rear tire goes flat, the back of your motorcycle may jerk or sway from side to side. Stop riding and check your tires right away if you feel this movement.

questions.question: If a sign prohibits mopeds on a freeway:

options.text: Mopeds cannot be used on the freeway.
Mopeds can be used only when traffic is moving smoothly.
Mopeds can be used if they go no faster than 25 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Mopeds cannot be used on the freeway.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to operate a moped on a freeway or expressway if signs prohibit it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Signal ahead
Crossroad ahead
Divided roadway ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that the road ahead is divided.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used in an emergency.
Should be used together with the rear brake.
Is unsafe to use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used together with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Where should your feet be when riding?

options.text: On the gas tank.
Hanging loose.
On the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the footrests.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests while riding. This helps you balance properly.

questions.question: What is the safest part of the lane?

options.text: Always the left side of the lane.
Always the right side of the lane.
It depends on the situation.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the situation.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always safest. Change your position based on road conditions and traffic.

questions.question: If a rider wears a helmet during a crash, are they more likely to survive?

options.text: No, they are less likely to survive.
No, survival chances are the same.
Yes, they are more likely to survive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, they are more likely to survive.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries than riders wearing helmets, regardless of speed.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?

options.text: Let them pass.
Speed up.
Keep riding normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass.
questions.explanation: The safest way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Speeding up will not help—they will just tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: What happens if you drink just one drink before riding?

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
It can affect your ability to ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect your ability to ride.
questions.explanation: Even one drink impairs your riding skills. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: What color are service signs?

options.text: Orange with black letters.
Blue with white letters.
Green with white letters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blue with white letters.
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. These include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: When riding in a group, how should riders use mirrors?

options.text: All riders should check mirrors often.
Only the lead rider should check mirrors.
Mirrors should not be checked often because they distract.

questions.correctAnswerText: All riders should check mirrors often.
questions.explanation: All riders in a group should check their mirrors regularly to see the riders behind them and make sure the group stays together.

questions.question: Where should a passenger sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: In front of the rider.
Sidesaddle.
Behind the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Behind the rider.
questions.explanation: Passengers must sit behind the rider and hold firmly onto the rider's waist or hips. They can hold onto handgrips if the motorcycle has them. Never sit sidesaddle.

questions.question: What should you do if you need to stop quickly?

options.text: Use the front brake only.
Use the front brake first.
Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply steady pressure to both brakes at the same time. Be careful not to lock the brakes.

questions.question: When stopping while carrying a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Ride a little faster than normal.
Begin slowing down earlier than normal.
Merge into smaller traffic gaps than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Begin slowing down earlier than normal.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle, making it slower to respond. It takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn. Begin slowing earlier, reduce your speed, and look for bigger gaps when turning or merging into traffic.
